title: Run and explain a Java program
subject: Java
core: Create BookStats.java with a main method. Given int[] pages = {120, 250, 80}, print the total and count of books with at least 100 pages.
stretch: Read three page counts from the console, reject negative values, and explain each variable's type.
checks: The sample prints total=450 and longBooks=2
An empty array produces zero totals
Explain the loop and run the program without AI-generated code
hints: Start with a total of zero and visit each array element.
Keep a second counter and increment it only when pages >= 100.
Use a for-each loop; update total on every iteration.
readingFocus: Language basics: variables, arrays, conditions and loops.

title: Extract methods and handle boundaries
subject: Java
core: Write static int totalPages(int[] pages). Call it with the sample from day 1 and an empty array. Decide and document how null input behaves.
stretch: Add countLongBooks(int[] pages, int minimum). Test zero and negative thresholds.
checks: totalPages({120,250,80}) returns 450
An empty array returns 0
Null input is rejected explicitly; explain return values versus printing
hints: Separate calculation from console output.
An accumulator belongs inside the method so each call starts fresh.
Objects.requireNonNull can make the null contract explicit.
readingFocus: Methods, parameters, return values and scope.

title: Model a book with an invariant
subject: Java
core: Create a Book record with long id, String title and String author. Reject non-positive ids and blank titles or authors in its constructor.
stretch: Build a console catalogue using three Book objects. Explain record immutability and equality.
checks: new Book(1,"Clean Code","Robert Martin") succeeds
A zero id, blank title or null author is rejected
Explain the difference between a type, an instance and a constructor
hints: Make invalid states fail at construction.
A record compact constructor can validate its components.
Check id <= 0, null strings, and isBlank before accepting input.
readingFocus: Object-oriented programming and records.

title: Find books in a list
subject: Java
core: Using the Book type from day 3, write Optional<Book> findById(List<Book> books, long id) using a loop.
stretch: Add findByAuthor without mutating the input list. Explain why the result should not expose mutable storage.
checks: An existing id returns its book
An absent id returns Optional.empty()
An empty list works; explain Optional without calling get blindly
hints: The search may not find a match; represent that in the return type.
Return immediately when a matching id is found.
Return Optional.of(book) on a match and Optional.empty() after the loop.
readingFocus: Collections: List iteration; Optional.

title: Add and delete without duplicate ids
subject: Java
core: Create an in-memory catalogue backed by Map<Long,Book>. Implement add(Book) and boolean delete(long id). Reject a duplicate id.
stretch: Add a list() method returning a defensive copy. Discuss why Map fits identifier lookups.
checks: Adding a new id makes it retrievable
A duplicate id is rejected without overwriting the first book
Delete returns true once and false for a missing id
hints: A map key should be the book id.
putIfAbsent distinguishes a new id from a duplicate.
remove(id) returns the removed value, or null when absent.
readingFocus: Collections: Map, keys, duplicates and defensive copies.

title: Debug a removal bug
subject: Java
core: Reproduce removing matching books from an ArrayList inside a for-each loop. Explain the failure, then implement removeByAuthor(List<Book>, String) safely.
stretch: Compare removeIf with an explicit Iterator. Demonstrate an input with adjacent matches.
checks: Every matching author is removed
Adjacent matches are not skipped
No ConcurrentModificationException occurs; explain why structural modification caused the original failure
hints: The for-each loop is using an iterator internally.
Use an API designed for removal while iterating.
books.removeIf(book -> book.author().equals(author)) is one safe option.
readingFocus: Collections iteration and exception stack traces.

title: Rebuild Java basics using expenses
subject: Java
core: Close earlier solutions. Write int totalPositive(int[] amounts): sum strictly positive values and ignore zero or negative values. Narrate your loop.
stretch: Build a console expense tracker with validation and a list command.
checks: An empty array returns 0
Rebuild from a blank file and explain the filtering condition
hints: Recall the accumulator from day 1, but change which values contribute.
Only add when amount > 0.
Initialise total to zero, loop once, and return the accumulator.
readingFocus: Recall before reading: variables, loops and methods.

title: Introduce an interface and a service
subject: Java
core: Define BookStore with findAll() and add(Book). Implement InMemoryBookStore. Write a BookService that receives BookStore through its constructor.
stretch: Add delete and a second fake implementation. Explain how constructor injection helps testing.
checks: The service can list and add through the interface
The service receives its dependency; it does not create the store
Explain interface versus implementation with your own code
hints: Start with the operations the service needs.
A constructor parameter can be an interface type.
Keep a final BookStore field and delegate to it.
readingFocus: Interfaces, constructors and dependency boundaries.

title: Filter and sort book titles
subject: Java
core: Write List<String> titlesByAuthor(List<Book>, String) that filters by exact author, returns titles alphabetically, and leaves the input unchanged.
stretch: Implement it once with loops and once with streams. Compare their readability.
checks: Only matching authors appear
Titles are sorted alphabetically
No matches returns an empty list and the source order is unchanged
hints: Think filter, transform, then sort.
map(Book::title) changes books into titles.
Chain filter, map, sorted and toList.
readingFocus: Collections and streams: filter, map and sorted.

title: Read sample JSON into books
subject: Java
core: In a Spring Boot project with JSON support, load books.json from src/main/resources into Book[]. Fixture: [{"id":1,"title":"Clean Code","author":"Robert Martin"},{"id":2,"title":"Effective Java","author":"Joshua Bloch"}]. Print both titles. Use the JSON mapper managed by your chosen Boot version.
stretch: Expose loading through a small reader class. Try an empty array, malformed JSON and a missing resource.
checks: The two supplied books deserialize with correct ids and titles
[] produces zero books
A missing file causes a clear error rather than silently pretending the catalogue is empty
hints: A classpath resource is different from a path relative to your shell.
Read an InputStream and tell the mapper the target array type.
Use getResourceAsStream("/books.json"), check for null, and readValue(stream, Book[].class).
readingFocus: JSON representation and Java records. Use your IDE's mapper API for the Boot version you selected.

title: Wire a service through Spring
subject: Spring Boot
core: Create a Boot application with @Service BookService and @RestController BookController. Inject the service through the controller constructor. Add GET /status returning {"status":"ready"}. Use port 8082 for your practice app.
stretch: Inject an in-memory store into the service. Explain component scanning and why manually creating BookService bypasses Spring.
checks: GET /status on port 8082 returns 200 and status=ready
The controller uses constructor injection
Explain where Spring discovers both classes
hints: Put components beneath the application package.
A single constructor does not need @Autowired.
Add server.port=8082 in application.properties to keep PATIPP's 8081 free.
readingFocus: Controller annotations and Java resource representation.

title: Serve the JSON catalogue
subject: Spring Boot
core: Extend yesterday's app: load the two-book fixture and implement GET /books through a service. Keep HTTP mapping in the controller and storage in the service.
stretch: Add GET /books/{id} with 404 for absent ids. Explain request -> controller -> service -> store.
checks: GET /books returns 200 and a JSON array containing both sample books
An empty catalogue returns []
The controller delegates instead of holding its own book list
hints: Reuse the reader from day 10.
A controller can return a List<Book>; Spring serializes it.
Load once during construction or initialization, then expose a defensive list copy.
readingFocus: Returning Java objects as JSON; adapt the greeting response to a list.

title: Add a book through POST
subject: Spring Boot
core: Implement POST /books accepting {"id":3,"title":"Refactoring","author":"Martin Fowler"}. Return 201 and the created book. Reject duplicate ids with 409. Use the existing service map.
stretch: Add Location: /books/{id}. Test blank titles and explain request DTOs versus stored records.
checks: A new id returns 201 and the submitted fields
A subsequent GET /books includes the new book
A duplicate returns 409 and does not replace existing data
hints: @RequestBody binds JSON to your Java input type.
Keep duplicate detection inside the service.
putIfAbsent plus a conflict exception avoids overwriting the existing book.
readingFocus: Request bodies, HTTP mappings and response representation.

title: Delete a book through DELETE
subject: Spring Boot
core: Implement DELETE /books/{id}. Return 204 with no body when removed and 404 for a missing id. Keep deletion in the service.
stretch: Use an HTTP client to prove that deleting one book leaves other books intact. Explain why repeated deletion can return 404.
checks: Deleting an existing id returns 204 with an empty body
The deleted book no longer appears in GET /books
Deleting an unknown id returns 404 and other books remain
hints: @PathVariable binds the id in the URL.
Map.remove returns null for a missing key.
Return ResponseEntity.noContent().build() after a successful service call.
readingFocus: HTTP mappings and path parameters.

title: Make bad requests predictable
subject: Spring Boot
core: Add a create-book DTO with @NotBlank title and author, and @Positive id. Apply @Valid to the POST request. Test one blank title and one malformed body. Ensure the validation starter is installed.
stretch: Add @RestControllerAdvice with a consistent problem response. Keep 400 validation errors distinct from 404 and 409.
checks: A blank title returns 400
Malformed JSON returns 400 rather than 500
Valid JSON still creates a book with 201
hints: Binding and validation are separate steps.
Use jakarta.validation annotations on the request DTO.
@Valid @RequestBody CreateBook request triggers constraint validation.
readingFocus: Use the web testing guide to assert status and response data; look up validation APIs in your IDE.

title: Test the API's behaviour
subject: Spring Boot
core: Write a web test for GET /books and POST /books. Assert status and JSON fields, not just that the application starts. Use the testing imports for your selected Boot version.
stretch: Add DELETE success, missing-id, duplicate-id and invalid-input tests. Explain what a slice test replaces compared with an integration test.
checks: GET has a test asserting 200 and a known title
POST has a test asserting 201 and the created id
Tests can run without manually starting the app
hints: MockMvc sends requests through Spring's web layer.
Use a known store state; each test should own its data.
perform(get("/books")).andExpect(status().isOk()) then assert a JSON path.
readingFocus: MockMvc, assertions and isolating the web layer.

title: Rebuild a small product API
subject: Spring Boot
core: Close the book code. In a fresh package, implement Product(id,name) with GET /products and DELETE /products/{id} over an in-memory map.
stretch: Rebuild GET, POST and DELETE from a fresh Boot project, then add validation and tests. Narrate all layers.
checks: GET returns the current products as an array
Deleting a seeded product returns 204
A missing id returns 404; implement without copying the book solution
hints: Identify the shared behaviour, then rename the domain.
Use a service map and constructor-injected controller.
Transfer the GET and remove patterns from memory; only inspect the reference after trying.
readingFocus: Recall the mappings before opening the guide.

title: Persist your first entity
subject: Spring Boot
core: Create a separate persistence practice app with Spring Data JPA and H2. Define a BookEntity class with a generated Long id and a protected no-argument constructor. Save and read a book through a repository in a test.
stretch: Wire the repository into a service and compare file-backed H2 or PostgreSQL with an in-memory database.
checks: Saving a book assigns a non-null id
Reading the saved id returns its title
Explain why a JPA entity is a class rather than reusing the immutable Book record
hints: Follow the JPA guide's entity and repository structure.
Use @Id @GeneratedValue and a no-argument constructor.
Extend JpaRepository<BookEntity,Long> and use save then findById.
readingFocus: Entity, id generation, repository and a repository test.

title: Map API data separately from entities
subject: Spring Boot
core: Add BookResponse(Long id,String title) and map a BookEntity into it in your service. Make GET return DTOs rather than entities.
stretch: Add CreateBookRequest and explain where input validation, persistence and response formatting belong.
checks: The response contains only id and title
Mapping preserves the stored values
The controller does not expose the JPA entity directly
hints: A response record describes the HTTP contract.
Mapping can be a small method before adding any mapping library.
new BookResponse(entity.getId(), entity.getTitle()) is sufficient.
readingFocus: Entity fields versus application response data.

title: Update inside a transaction
subject: Spring Boot
core: Add rename(long id,String title) to the persistence service. Reject blank titles, find the entity or return 404, and update inside @Transactional.
stretch: Add a test that a rejected update leaves the prior title intact. Explain dirty checking and transaction boundaries.
checks: Renaming an existing book is observable on a later read
A missing book returns 404
A blank title is rejected without altering the stored title
hints: Place the transaction on the service operation.
Load the entity before changing its title.
A managed entity's change is written when the transaction commits.
readingFocus: Repository operations and transaction boundaries.

title: Test persistence with isolated data
subject: Spring Boot
core: Write a repository test that saves two books, deletes one and verifies the other still exists. Do not depend on test execution order.
stretch: Add a service integration test for rename and missing-id behaviour. Explain rollback between tests.
checks: Two saved books get distinct ids
Deleting one id does not remove the other
The test passes when run alone and repeatedly
hints: Each test should create its own starting data.
Use ids returned by save instead of assuming 1 and 2.
Check existsById for both records after deleteById.
readingFocus: Repository testing with an embedded database.

title: Return deliberate error responses
subject: Spring Boot
core: Introduce BookNotFoundException and translate it to a 404 ProblemDetail in @RestControllerAdvice. Keep internal exception details out of the response.
stretch: Add validation and duplicate-conflict responses, and tests for their status and stable fields.
checks: A missing book yields HTTP 404
The response has a human-readable detail
A normal GET still returns the successful DTO
hints: A domain exception can be translated at the HTTP boundary.
@ExceptionHandler selects the exception to translate.
ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail creates the response without a custom error framework.
readingFocus: HTTP response contracts; inspect ProblemDetail in your framework API.

title: Search by title with a query parameter
subject: Spring Boot
core: Add GET /books?title=java that filters titles case-insensitively. An absent parameter returns all books; no match returns [].
stretch: Move filtering into a repository query for persisted data. Test spaces and mixed case.
checks: A mixed-case query matches titles regardless of case
An absent query returns all books
A query with no matches returns 200 and []
hints: A query parameter is not a path variable.
Normalise both query and title using Locale.ROOT.
Use @RequestParam(required=false) and a filtering service method.
readingFocus: Optional request parameters and response mapping.

title: Paginate a stable collection
subject: Java
core: Write <T> List<T> page(List<T> values,int offset,int limit). Reject negative offsets and non-positive limits. Return an empty list beyond the end.
stretch: Expose pagination on GET /books and keep ordering stable. Explain why result limits matter.
checks: An offset beyond the end returns []
Invalid arguments are rejected and the returned list is a copy
hints: Compute start and end within the list bounds.
Beware overflow when offset + limit is large.
Bound the requested length by values.size() - start before adding.
readingFocus: Collections: subList, copies and generics.

title: Debug the wrong HTTP mapping
subject: Spring Boot
core: Deliberately annotate a delete handler with @GetMapping("/books/{id}"). Reproduce why DELETE receives 405, fix the mapping, and add a regression test.
stretch: Use a breakpoint to trace an HTTP request through controller and service. Log only useful, non-sensitive values.
checks: The corrected DELETE returns 204 for an existing id
GET /books does not delete anything
A regression test fails for the broken mapping and passes after the fix
hints: A URL alone does not identify an HTTP operation.
Compare the method sent by the client with the annotation.
Use @DeleteMapping for deletion and assert it with MockMvc.delete.
readingFocus: MockMvc requests and response status assertions.

title: Transfer persistence to a task tracker
subject: Spring Boot
core: Without opening the book implementation, define TaskEntity(id,description,done) and a repository. Save a task, mark it done and read it back.
stretch: Build GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /tasks with DTOs, validation and tests.
checks: A saved task receives an id and starts unfinished
Marking it done survives a later read
Explain the entity/repository/service boundaries without copying book code
hints: Identify the concept that transfers: generated id and stored fields.
Use a boolean field for done and a domain method to change it.
Inside a transaction, load the entity and call markDone().
readingFocus: Recall entity and repository design before reopening the guide.

title: A short Java interview drill
subject: Java
core: After untimed practice, try a 15-minute drill: implement firstUnique(List<String>) returning the first value appearing once, or Optional.empty(). Explain your choice of collection.
stretch: Repeat with case-insensitive matching, then write tests. If the timed attempt feels premature, use untimed practice.
checks: [a,b,a,c] returns b
[a,a] and [] return Optional.empty()
Explain the time and space costs and test before declaring completion
hints: You need counts and original encounter order.
Count with a LinkedHashMap, then find the first count of 1.
merge(value,1,Integer::sum) builds the counts in one pass.
readingFocus: Attempt from memory first; review Map only after the drill.

title: A short Spring interview drill
subject: Spring Boot
core: After practising the underlying concepts, rebuild DELETE /products/{id} with a service-backed map in 20 minutes. Return 204 on success and 404 when absent. Narrate the request path.
stretch: Spend 60 minutes rebuilding GET/POST/DELETE and two tests from a fresh project. Stay untimed if you still need the reference.
checks: The controller delegates to a constructor-injected service
An existing product is removed with 204
A missing product returns 404; explain how the id reaches the service
hints: Write the service operation before the controller.
Use @PathVariable long id and @DeleteMapping.
Map.remove plus a missing-id exception expresses the core behaviour.
readingFocus: Attempt the mapping and service boundary before reading.

title: Build a small app feature end to end
subject: Spring Boot
core: Choose your books or tasks app. Implement one previously missing operation through request DTO, controller, service and storage, and add one behavioural test.
stretch: Complete the app's create/list/delete operations, errors, validation and tests. Write a README with exact commands and sample requests.
checks: The chosen operation works through an HTTP request
A test verifies the successful result and a failure case
You can explain the code you wrote and identify any assistance used
hints: Choose one thin feature instead of rewriting the whole project.
Write expected HTTP input/output before implementation.
Trace one request across the layers and test it at the boundary.
readingFocus: Review only the testing section needed for your chosen operation.

title: Rebuild, explain and choose your next focus
subject: Spring Boot
core: Close your earlier implementation. Rebuild a tiny in-memory Book service with add and delete, including duplicate and missing-id behaviour. Record one remaining weakness.
stretch: In 90–120 minutes rebuild a fresh Book API with JSON loading, GET/POST/DELETE, validation and tests. Explain it without reading the source. Compare day 1 and day 30 evidence.
checks: A new book can be added and deleted
A duplicate is rejected and a missing delete is reported
You rebuild from a blank file, explain your choices and name the next concept to revisit
hints: Recall the map operations before thinking about annotations.
Separate the Java service from HTTP mapping.
Use putIfAbsent for add and remove for delete; wire mappings only after the service works.
readingFocus: Recall first; revisit only the concept identified in your reflection.
